title: Digital, climate-sensitive heart failure management in general practice
summary: Heart failure (HF) is a major public health problem, causing 37,570 deaths annually in Germany and becoming increasingly common in the elderly population (over 15% of those aged 75 and older are affected). Chronic heart failure severely restricts the quality of life of patients, leading to symptoms such as fatigue, shortness of breath, and fluid retention. Although the general practitioner plays a central role in treatment, official therapy recommendations are often insufficiently implemented. To close these care gaps, the study uses the digital PIA-HF-ICT solution, which securely connects a patient app and a practice system (GDPR-compliant via the UKB cloud), with the main goal of improving the quality of life and care for patients and detecting an early deterioration of health status to prevent hospital admissions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients:
Stable Chronic Heart Failure (ICD-10: I50.-)
Age is ≥ 18
Stage II-IIIEmergency treatment in a practice, emergency room, and/or hospital due to HF (Heart Failure) in the last 2 years
Uses a smart device ≥ 3x/week
Ejection fraction < 50
Understands study documentationInsured under the statutory health insurance (GKV-versichert)

Practice Staff:
The physician is certified as a specialist in general medicine (Facharzt für Allgemeinmedizin), a general practitioner-level internist, or a general practitioner Practice treats patients with heart failure
Practice has ≥ 1 MFA
Exclusion criteria:
Patients:
Cognitive impairments
(Planned) cardiac assist devices (e.g., VADs)
Pregnancy/breastfeeding
Dialysis
Other severe illness

Practice Staff:
Practice is specialized in cardiology/Group practice (Gemeinschaftspraxis)
Practice has no internet access
